doc.title: Ed Polcer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998

chapter: Swing Street shows and the business
title: Playing overseas and entertaining audiences
summary: He describes appreciative audiences in Europe and Japan, a six-month stay in Paris in 1963, and jazzmen as entertainers.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: How about playing overseas like in Europe?

Very appreciative audiences. I tried living in Paris for six months and living there on European musician’s terms is not economically very good. This is a while ago when I lived — this is 1963, and I mean I was working for eight dollars a night and fifteen dollars a night. I tried living in Paris for six months and traveling around Europe. But going over there as an American with pre-booked gigs, you’re getting the best of everything. You’re treated nicely and the audiences really do love you. Japan the same way. But I’ve had a good run here in the States, because of the narrative and because of being friendly with the audiences. I mean I think every audience I play for I have a good time and I think they do.
There’s a lot to be said for giving the audience credit and wanting to include them in what you’re doing. I mean jazz musicians considered themselves entertainers, didn’t they?

Yeah. I mean you see what the Ellington band wore and the way that the sections would move, if it was good enough for them it’s good enough for me. I mean what’s this stand up here and be a hero bologna? Let’s have some fun. Let’s get into it.
